title: Canonical rank-one comparison for intrinsic pro-etale constant modules
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and a finite commutative ring $A$, use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and its constant commutative ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Write $M_X=A_X$ as its own ordinary module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], using Mathlib's rank-one module, and $C_X$ for the constant fixed-scalar sheaf of the rank-one $A$-module. Let $E_X$ be the canonical intrinsic coefficient realization used in [def-weil-extension-by-zero], obtained by module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] along the constant-scalar unit; use its scalar-unit section map from [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Define $c_X:E_X(C_X)\simeq M_X$ to be the unique module-sheaf isomorphism whose component sends the realization of every constant section $a\in A$ on every site object to the same scalar section of $A_X$. Such a unique isomorphism exists: both successive sheafifications have the same underlying associated abelian sheaf and the same constant scalar action. This defines the canonical rank-one comparison, including for the zero ring and the empty scheme.
